questions.stemHtml: A 35-year-old male patient comes to the clinic complaining of a hypopigmented scaly patch on his upper back as shown in the picture below, that has been present for the past 3 months. He denies any associated itching, pain, or other symptoms. On physical examination, the patch is non-tender, and has well-defined borders. There are no similar lesions elsewhere on his body. The rest of the examination is unremarkable. What is the most appropriate next step in the evaluation of this patient?
